sponges text index | photo index Phylum Porifera Black antler sponge Haliclona sp.*
Family Chalinidaeupdated Oct 2016

Where seen? This black sponge that resembles antles is sometimes seen on our Northern shores, growing on hard surfaces, including pipes and abandoned drums near the mid-water mark. Features: Sparsely branching ‘stems’ (up to 20cm long) that are cylindrical thick (about 3-4cm in diameter) with a smooth surface. Some branches taper to elegant points. Also with low knobs. Holes at the top of knobs, and along the length of the ‘stems’. Colour usually a deep black, but when exposed out of water may be greyish.


Changi, Jul 07


Pulau Sekudu, Aug 05


Changi, Jul 10

*Species are difficult to positively identify without close examination.
On this website, they are grouped by external features for convenience of display.
